strengths: Well-motivated core observation: convincing empirical evidence that KV states exhibit strong energy concentration in low-frequency DCT components (Figure 1), supported by perturbation analysis (Figure 2) and summarization experiments (Table 1)
Parameter-free and architecture-agnostic design: no additional trainable parameters or architectural modifications required, enabling broad applicability across model variants

Comprehensive and strong empirical validation: SOTA on most LongBench tasks, only method maintaining performance at 16K beyond original window (Table 4, RULER), substantial improvements on long-context generation (LongGenBench)
Remarkable extrapolation capability: extends LLaMA-2-7B from 8K to 256K tokens (64×) while maintaining stable perplexity, demonstrating effective iterative compression strategy
Significant practical efficiency: 40.89% faster training and 44.19% less memory than full fine-tuning (Table 7), with negligible compression overhead (<0.3%) during inference
Robust under aggressive compression: remains stable even at extreme γ=1% retaining ratio (Table 3) while other methods degrade sharply, demonstrating method robustness

Thorough experimental rigor: extensive ablations (Appendix F), head-wise analysis (Appendix B), careful comparison with variants (Dropping), and analysis of key design choices (rescaling factor, RoPE integration)
Clear presentation with effective visualizations: Figure 3 clearly illustrates frequency compression pipeline, Figure 4 heatmaps effectively demonstrate failure modes of baselines
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core technique is standard DCT-based low-pass filtering applied to KV cache; the innovation is somewhat incremental and primarily engineering-focused rather than algorithmic

Significant performance degradation on formula-heavy text: Proof-pile results (Table 9) show FreqKV trails LongLoRA substantially at 32K context (2.72 vs 2.50), revealing fundamental limitation where local details of symbolic content are critical

Incomplete semantic understanding: while Figure 2 demonstrates low-frequency robustness, limited analysis of what semantic information is actually preserved; beyond summarization (Table 1), sparse investigation of which task types benefit from global vs. local information

Weak performance on specific task categories: few-shot learning tasks show minimal gains or slight regression (Table 3: TRECL 56.0 vs 75.5 full cache), lacking analysis of which downstream tasks degrade most under compression

RoPE integration lacks theoretical justification: decision to compress before rather than after RoPE is empirically motivated (Table 8) but conceptually unclear; explanation of avoiding 'out-of-bound position embeddings' needs rigorous technical argument; potential fragility with alternative position encodings

Hyperparameter choices inadequately justified: default γ=0.5 not well motivated (ablations show γ=0.75 improves performance), sink size S=4 appears arbitrary with limited sensitivity analysis (only three γ values tested), missing guidance on selection

Theory-practice gap: limited explanation of why DCT specifically is appropriate for transformer KV states versus alternatives (FFT, wavelets); insufficient analysis of relationship between observed frequency properties and underlying attention mechanics

Comparison fairness issues: baseline OOM at extended lengths (Table 2) complicates direct comparison; some results reproduced by authors (marked with *) potentially introducing inconsistencies; no direct comparison with position interpolation methods under identical conditions
Missing failure mode analysis: limited guidance on when practitioners should prefer alternative approaches; few-shot learning degradation suggests domain-dependent utility not fully characterized
Position encoding claims need stronger support: Section 3.4 claims about avoiding position extrapolation deserve more rigorous technical justification rather than empirical verification alone
